sentences.text: The upper jaw of this extinct bird measures exactly 7.0 mm in length.
Its nostril opening is roughly thirty percent larger than that of modern cowbirds.
A distinct, even curve runs along the top of its beak, a feature unique among icterids.
The species Pandanaris convexa was first described in 1947 by scientist Alden H. Miller.
The initial fossils were unearthed at the La Brea Tar Pits in California.
This bird lived in grasslands where it ate insects disturbed by large animals.
Scientists believe it likely evolved alongside Pleistocene megafauna.
Pandanaris is a genus containing only this single species.
The animal existed from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
It is debated whether Pandanaris went fully extinct because it was wholly dependent on megafaunal communities and could not tolerate altered habitats.
